rationale: Reviewed cb272d508cfe1ef85582e9cea6c085bb196bbc63, the revised spec, ADR-0045 and its back-pointers, against the G3 R4/R6 adversarial lens. All three of my round-1 asks are addressed in the revised contract. Two new design gaps remain: the reachable fallback cannot enforce its destination restriction for the destination-free subject it explicitly admits, and hashing the current first-failure Detail does not prevent an override from covering additional failures hidden behind that first failure. Three scratch-only probes passed, reproducing these gaps; the fallback probes emulate only the proposed candidate generator through an existing seam, not an implementation of unshipped code. Twelve selected existing landing safeguards also passed. Both relevant refutations were checked, including real bd 1.1.0 ready-row measurements. The source repository was not modified; all fixtures and tests are in scratch. GH issue 239 could not be independently read because api.github.com was unreachable; no independent issue-content claim is made.
concrete_changes_required: Resolve R4.2's destination-free candidate contract before approval. `Merge bead/<id>` proves no destination, and gitutil.MergeInto emits that subject for any targetWorkdir. Do not call that form target-pinned or promise to exclude other-bead/spec destinations on its text alone. Define an implementable policy for these historical merges (additional target provenance or an explicitly bounded reachability policy), reconcile the ADR-0041 amendment, and pin the intended outcome in MF-3 AND reattest. Extend AC-11 with (1) short-form X->Y followed only by Y reaching spec/S and (2) short-form X(old tip)->Y, X(new tip)->spec/S, then the off-first-parent topology. The former must not silently bypass the chosen destination policy; the latter must identify the genuine landing rather than inherit spurious different-second-parent ambiguity from the sibling merge.

Make R6.2/R6.4's stored authorization fingerprint account for all failures within a signal, rather than only its current first rendered Detail. Price any signal/API changes required, for example complete canonical failure sets or a conservative context fingerprint. Extend AC-16/AC-17 with persistence tests that record an override for failing dependency A, retain A unchanged and add failing dependency B, and require ready-check to refuse until fresh evidence is recorded. Add the analogous MF-4 case retaining the first blocker while adding another blocker/checklist failure. Keep the already-specified no-flagless-reclaim and explicit narrower-request rules.

findings.title: Round-1 ask status
findings.detail: G3.1 ADDRESSED: R4.1 no longer delegates membership to FindEpicForBead or a ready set; it defines status-independent plan-ID OR metadata.spec_id OR a parent read, excludes titles, and fails closed on read/parse errors. AC-10(d)/(f)/(g) pins metadata-only, title-only and indeterminate cases. R1.1/OQ-9 deliberately narrow selection to plan beads, so the old unsupported metadata-only claim promise is removed; AC-1/AC-2 pin that boundary and its valid repair. G3.2 ADDRESSED: R6.3 explicitly classifies schema-v2 VALID, evidence-less LEGACY and MALFORMED markers; R6.2 disallows flagless claim reuse entirely, and AC-17 pins legacy/malformed/read-error negatives. Evidence text omission and no read-time file re-verification are explicit policies, rather than accidental legacy authorization. G3.3 ADDRESSED: AC-16 now asserts that named-but-passing IDs are not persisted, subsequent MF-2 failure is uncovered, flagless reclaim refuses, and a narrower explicit request cannot union an existing marker; AC-15 pins invalid IDs before mutation. The two findings below are NEW_ISSUE regressions/gaps in the revised R4.2 and R6 digest designs, not missed round-1 asks.

findings.title: NEW_ISSUE: the short-form fallback cannot pin its merge destination
findings.detail: spec.md:250-255 admits exact `Merge bead/<id>` while saying it excludes merges into another bead/spec branch; the ADR Touchpoints amendment likewise requires the spec branch as target. internal/gitutil/gitops.go:315's MergeInto actually formats `Merge <sourceBranch>` for whatever branch targetWorkdir has checked out. TestG3R2TargetlessWrongDestinationAdmitted uses that real primitive to merge X into Y, then merges only Y into spec/S. Today's FindLandedMerge(X) returns NoCandidate. Emulating precisely the proposed R4.2 generator makes FindLandedMerge(X) succeed and return the X->Y merge, corroborated by X's exact surviving tip, with no forged panel, binding or subject. Reachability does not recover the omitted historical destination. TestG3R2TargetlessSiblingMakesRealLandingAmbiguous then advances X, lands the new tip on S, lands Y, and moves the real landing off first-parent: the admitted short-form sibling merge contributes an older second parent and the unchanged grouping rule refuses the real landing as ambiguous. AC-11(iii)'s explicit `into bead/Y` example misses both boundaries. Probe source: scratch repo/internal/lifecycle/g3_round2_probe_test.go.

findings.title: NEW_ISSUE: a first-failure digest still widens dispatch override coverage
findings.detail: spec.md:316 and :330 hash the signal's rendered Detail and conclude that an override for one failure never covers a different failure under the same signal ID. The current API does not supply a complete failure identity: evaluateMF3 returns immediately on its first failing dependency (readiness.go:635-641 and each landed-error arm), and evaluateMF4 returns its first blocking token before checking other tokens/checklist failures (readiness.go:845-863). No R4/R6 requirement changes that behavior. TestG3R2AddedFailureKeepsOverrideDigest proves that deps=[open A] and deps=[open A,open B] produce byte-identical rendered MF-3 Detail and SHA-256, and likewise one TBD line vs that unchanged line plus a new TBD line for MF-4. Under R6.4's exact written rule, the existing VALID marker still covers the signal and ready-check exits 0, authorizing dispatch despite the newly added unapproved failure. Fresh flags protect a new claim but do not protect this dispatch-ingress read-back. AC-17 only replaces the first dependency, which changes Detail and misses the masking case. Probe source: scratch repo/internal/validate/readiness/g3_round2_probe_test.go.

findings.title: Refutations and retained landing safeguards
findings.detail: The registerLandedPanel refutation is correct: internal/validate/readiness/fixtures.go:189 defines it; its fixed slug explains the requested AC-12 extension. The ready-row refutation is also independently reproduced on bd 1.1.0 (8e4e59d39) in scratch/bd-fixture: the created child row includes parent plus metadata.spec_id, while the parentless metadata-only row includes metadata and omits parent (measured-rows.json). R4.3 still requires exact second-parent equality and explicitly preserves surviving-tip/binding vetoes, so a matching stale/abandoned registration is not by itself a new candidate-generation authority. Twelve existing tests passed for spoofed second parents, ancestor-only panels, forged/other-bead/anonymous bindings, inconsistent binding pairs, reverts, reapply and oldest-anchored masked reverts. These are baseline safeguards, not execution of the unimplemented panel-set reader.

findings.title: Errors in this BRIEF
findings.detail: The Summary still says to review both artifacts with `git show 7a490064`, and Reviewer conduct still suggests `git worktree add ... 7a490064`; Round 2 correctly supersedes the old SHA with cb272d50. The worktree command would also mutate the read-only source repository's git administrative state; I used the direct task's scratch clone. Acceptance criteria says there are 18 ACs, but the revised spec has AC-1 through AC-19. Round 2's stated 95-ask disposition arithmetic (91 fixed + 2 refuted + 0 deferred) totals 93. The header's beside-BRIEF verdict destination is explicitly overridden later, so I followed the exact scratch/verdict.json destination. These are brief hygiene issues, not additional gate-blocking changes.
